v.why: Replacing a missing direct input-output edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole strong path, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
A skip already provides a useful direct path, so upgrading it to a conv gains less than the average replacement.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 and the output, so adding a conv where there was none removes the main bottleneck.
Replacing a weak pooling op with a conv gives a bigger improvement than replacing an already-capable op.
Filling an empty edge with a learnable op gives a larger gain than modifying an existing op.
Removing a strong conv costs more accuracy than removing an average op (floor effect, a lower and more negative effect).
Deleting a conv on a main output edge hurts more than deleting a weak op.
Removing a weak pooling op costs little or even helps, so the effect is higher than when removing a useful op.
With a strong direct conv path already present, an extra conv on edge 4 has diminishing returns (ceiling).
With edge 1 removed, the 0->2->3 route is cut, so an upgraded edge 5 is less useful.
Edge 1 mainly reaches the output through edge 5, so a conv on edge 1 is wasted when edge 5 is absent.
Edge 0 reaches the output via edges 4 and 2->5, so losing edge 4 cuts one of its main routes.
Edge 2 only reaches the output through edge 5, so a conv there is useless without it.
Adding a direct identity path to an empty edge gives a large gain from the gradient and information shortcut.
A strong conv path through node 1 already fills the role, so the added 1x1 on the direct edge gains less.
A strong conv into the output already exists, so a second conv path is partly redundant (ceiling).
Edge 4 takes its input from node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so upgrading it is useless.
Upgrading a weak pooling op to a 3x3 conv gives a bigger gain than upgrading the average existing op.
Connecting node 1 to node 2 where there was none adds a new route and gives a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Adding a learnable op to an empty edge gives a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
